image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a vintage audio cassette tape. The casing is black plastic with a white paper label on the top face featuring red handwritten text and some printed black text. Two circular windows reveal the white spools inside, connected by dark magnetic tape. The bottom edge shows the rectangular opening for the tape head and write-protect tabs.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The red handwritten text is stylized and somewhat illegible, resembling graffiti. While this could be intentional artistic style, AI often struggles with coherent handwriting, resulting in 'fake' script that looks like letters but isn't quite right. The printed black text below it is also blurry and indistinct.

The texture of the magnetic tape inside the bottom slot appears slightly smudged or overly smooth, lacking the fine linear grain expected of magnetic tape. The reflection on the plastic near the bottom left corner is slightly diffuse and inconsistent with the sharper highlights elsewhere.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is indeed a cassette and not a similar rectangular plastic object (e.g., VHS adapter, generic box).
To analyze the legibility and coherence of the red handwritten text and black printed text, checking for AI-generated gibberish.
To verify the structural integrity of the plastic shell, ensuring no melting or fusion between the label, casing, and internal spools.
To assess general sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle global artifacts like noise patterns or unnatural blur.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of the handwritten red text on the label.
Structural correctness of the spool mechanism and tape path.
Boundary sharpness between the paper label and the plastic casing.
Realism of reflections on the curved plastic surfaces.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'handwritten' text. AI often generates pseudo-text that looks like writing from a distance but fails character-level inspection. Also, verify if the tape tension between the spools looks physically plausible or if it appears to float/melt into the casing.
